title: Ansel and the Escarpment
premise: Desert ranger Isandro Marchetti chases a thief, Ansel, who stole not money but a ledger proving the upriver concession company falsified water rights and let an expedition die in the escarpment. When Isandro's own radio goes silent and the expedition's last survivors signal from above the snowline, he realizes Ansel stole the truth to force a reckoning no court will grant. Together they cross the range ahead of the first snows to deliver the ledger before the permits expire at season's end. Isandro must choose between his oath to return the thief and his loyalty to the dead; they reach the valley as the passes close behind them, the ledger published, the permits voided, and Isandro surrendering his badge rather than arrest the man who saved him.
about_author: Edmund Zhou is a former surveyor who spent six seasons mapping arid river basins before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about landscapes that outlast every claim made upon them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Stopping
chapters.summary: Isandro Marchetti tracks a thief across the salt flats, three days into a pursuit he can't afford to abandon. POV: Isandro. The emotional beat is weary compulsion—the sense that stopping costs more than moving, even as the trail grows strange: the thief leaves water for him at each camp.

chapters.title: What Ansel Took
chapters.summary: Isandro corners Ansel at a dry well, but the stolen goods aren't coin—they're a concession ledger documenting falsified water rights and an expedition written off as lost. POV: Ansel. The beat is defiant grief: her brother was on that expedition, and the company buried the paperwork with the men.

chapters.title: Silence on the Upriver Band
chapters.summary: A distress call from the escarpment expedition—still alive, still waiting—cuts off mid-transmission. Isandro realizes the company jammed the frequency years ago and someone just broke through. POV: Isandro. The beat is dawning horror: staying invisible was never an option; the desert has been listening all along.

chapters.title: An Uneasy Truce
chapters.summary: Isandro releases Ansel from custody in exchange for her knowledge of the old survey routes through the escarpment. They ride together toward the range, company scouts shadowing them. POV: alternating. The beat is brittle trust—two people bound by different debts to the same dead men.

chapters.title: The Company's Men
chapters.summary: Company riders ambush them at a river ford, burning supplies and revealing the stakes: if the ledger surfaces before permit renewal, the concession collapses. POV: Ansel. The beat is cold fury sharpening into resolve—she stops running and starts planning.

chapters.title: Foot of the Escarpment
chapters.summary: They reach the range as autumn storms gather, finding the abandoned base camp and evidence the 'lost' expedition survived longer than reported—and were abandoned deliberately. POV: Isandro. The beat is moral rupture: his badge has been protecting the wrong side all along.

chapters.title: The Switchbacks
chapters.summary: A brutal climb through switchbacks as the first snows fall early. A scout attack forces them onto an unmapped ledge route; Isandro nearly dies holding the line so Ansel can pass. POV: Isandro. The beat is sacrifice offered without apology—loyalty shifting from institution to person.

chapters.title: Above the Snowline
chapters.summary: They find the expedition survivors in a high cave, led by a dying foreman who kept the second copy of the ledger hidden for two years. POV: Ansel. The beat is grief transfigured—her brother's final entries confirm everything, and the survivors choose to descend with them.

chapters.title: Race Before the Passes Close
chapters.summary: The descent becomes a race against closing weather and closing law: the company files an injunction and riders block the southern pass. The group takes the river gorge instead, hauling the injured through floodwater. POV: alternating. The beat is desperate collective will—strangers becoming a single rope-line.

chapters.title: What the Valley Decides
chapters.summary: They reach the valley as the passes seal shut behind them; the ledger reaches the land board, the permits expire unrenewed, and the company's men stand down. Isandro offers his badge rather than arrest Ansel. POV: Isandro. The beat is quiet justice outside the law—and the first rest either of them has taken in years.
